newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: INSTANT VIEW-RBNZ easing signal seen as positive.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW-RBNZ easing signal seen as positive.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash's sanctioning of a 100 basis point easing in monetary conditions was greeted positively by economists.
The following reactions have been gathered.
JASON WONG, ECONOMIST, FIRST NEW ZEALAND CAPITAL
"It's very positive for the market, slightly softer than markets expectations.
"The growth is obviously less optimistic than Treasury's, we expected that, but nevertheless, in their own right they are still quite bullish on growth and more so that the consensus forecast.

"With that, they have a lower inflation track than consensus forecasts. Most people around the market are sceptical of their track for the real monetary conditions indicator -- which remains flat for the next few years.
"Given the downside risks on the recovery developing, there is a very good chance that monetary conditions by much smaller than the bank has indicated," Wong said.
Wong said markets would take the MCI index to the extreme of the bank's tolerance level if the market has the view that conditions should be easier than the bank had indicated.
PAUL STEWART, CHIEF ECONMIST AT ANZ BANK
"We were a little surprised they've sanctioned so much easing at this point in time.

"The other surprising feature is that in the profile, although they have a further easing in the December quarter, they then have a tightening as early as March (1998). We might have anticipated a period of flat monetary conditions before

He said the market had taken monetary conditions as low as the Reserve Bank would allow at this stage, given that the bank indicated there was a 50 MCI point buffer either side of its preferred level.
He said he did not see the market taking conditions any lower at this stage.
"The next key event is the June quarter CPI.

"The Reserve Bank is picking 0.3 percent, and that's consitent with our own forecast, but obviously if it were to come in somewhat lower than that, then that again might improve the inflation outlook further and the market might push conditions a bit lower."
